against.text: Britain's Condign study found no evidence either of intelligent control of the objects, alleged inspections of UK strategic assets or any hostility or threat, and recommended ending the monitoring.

The Soviet programme's own history reports no landing, contact or abduction in thirteen years and concludes that either the USSR was closed to alien visits or the extraterrestrial hypothesis fails; it attributes the Petrozavodsk phenomenon to a satellite launch.

Canada's defence committee on the subject, Project Second Storey, met six times from 1952 to 1954 and concluded that UFOs posed no security threat and were of no scientific interest, recommending that military investigation end.

The model offices resolve most of what they receive: only 3.2 percent of GEIPAN's 3,188 cases remained unidentified, and GEIPAN's own current figure for its unexplained class is lower than the 4 to 5 percent COMETA gave in 1999.

Brazil's famous cases have conventional readings on its own record: a 2010 military inquiry concluded the Varginha witnesses saw a local man crouched by a wall, and a federal court in 2023 upheld dismissal of a suit to release Operacao Prato film, finding the claim of surviving film rested mainly on press reports and witness accounts.

Where offices disagreed on a single case, a conventional answer emerged: French analysts working through GEIPAN proposed a medium-haul aircraft venting cabin wastewater for the 2014 Chilean Navy footage, which CEFAA rejected, and independent analysts later matched the footage to scheduled flights.

answer.text: Britain handled reports through a Ministry of Defence desk that fed the defence intelligence section DI55. Its Project Condign study found no evidence of intelligent control, inspections of UK strategic assets or any threat, and recommended that DI55 stop monitoring reports; the desk closed in December 2009 and the files went to the National Archives.

France has studied the subject inside its space agency, CNES, since 1977, as GEPAN, then SEPRA and since 2005 GEIPAN, which publishes its case files; about 3.1 to 3.2 percent of its cases remain unidentified, and it says it is not a research group on UFOs or extraterrestrial life.

According to the history co-written by Yury Platov, who was the academic branch's chief executive, the Soviet Union ran a state programme on anomalous phenomena from 1978 to 1990 that registered about 3,000 messages, resolved more than 90 percent of events as rocket launches or balloons, and recorded no landing, contact or abduction.

Canada's Sky Canada Project of 2025 found reports scattered across departments and recommended a dedicated public service, naming the processes of the United States, France and Chile as examples; Chile has run an open civil-aviation office since 1997 and publishes its resolved cases.

for.text: Brazil's Air Defence Command, reporting on the night of 19 May 1986 when air force fighters pursued objects across four states, gave its opinion that the phenomena were solid and reflected a form of intelligence, by their capacity to follow and keep distance from observers and to fly in formation. The report was released only in 2009.

BBC Brasil reports that on 23 May 1986 Brazil's Minister of Aeronautics, with the five pilots and the controllers present, said five fighters had pursued 21 UFOs and that the episode would be investigated.

COMETA's 1999 report, written by a private association whose members included generals and an admiral, not by a government body, concluded that the studies show the almost certain physical reality of unknown flying objects apparently operated by intelligent beings, that secret earthly craft can explain only a minority of cases, and that the extraterrestrial hypothesis alone accounts for the facts.

Britain's Condign judged that the Soviet effort may well have been related to a programme of understanding and exploiting certain UAP-related natural phenomena such as plasmas, and critics quoted in another account allege that the Soviet academic branch was cover for a more serious military one.

Canada's Wilbert Smith wrote in a November 1950 memorandum that the subject was classified higher in the United States than the hydrogen bomb; a secondary account says he learned this from the US scientist Robert Sarbacher.
On the board's reading, Condign's flat denial of any US or Canadian intelligence exchange is oddly followed by four redacted lines, since a complete negative needs no withheld continuation.

lead.text: Britain's defence intelligence study and Canada's defence committee found no threat, the Soviet programme's academic history records no landing, contact or abduction, and France and Chile run open offices that publish their findings. The exceptions are Brazil's Air Defence Command, which in 1986 called the objects its fighters chased solid and showing a form of intelligence, and COMETA, a private French association whose members included generals and an admiral, which in 1999 favoured the extraterrestrial hypothesis.
